summary.intent: Plan, execute, and ship phase 64 of CipherBox — 'Rotation Soundness — Revocation Guarantees' — filling four throwing engine stubs and fixing three confirmed D-series bugs in the read-key rotation BFS walk.
summary.outcome: All 8 plans executed (TDD throughout, 297 unit tests green, 4/4 sdk-e2e green), ship-phase pipeline completed through CodeRabbit triage and low-risk fixes applied; PR body drafted but merge left to user.

repo: engine.ts `sealChildReadKey` call at L344-350 had a misnomer: `parentReadKey` parameter was actually the child's own pre-rotation key; the fix (D-02) belongs out-of-band in the BFS caller under the parent's NEW readKey', not inside rotateOne itself

registration.ts L174-175 had silent fallbacks `nodeId: params.nodeId ?? crypto.randomUUID()` and `generation: params.nodeGeneration ?? 0` that silently broke AAD stability and generation convergence tests across all 6 `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` call sites in client.ts

`PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY` in engine.ts's `sealNode` serves the write-body seal role (0x04) and is legitimately Phase 65 scope — it is NOT the D-01 fail-closed target; the IPNS publish key path is separate and now guarded by a throw

Design §4.5 explicitly states double-rotation IS the safe crash-recovery path ('an extra rotation only strengthens revocation'); SC#4's 'without double-bumping' wording directly contradicts the design, making the 64-07 no-double-bump guard an over-constraint

The root node has no parent mirror, so the convergence guard (per-node generation check) cannot skip an already-rotated root during a fresh-record resume — this requires the Phase-68 durable client floor

`verifySubtreeClean` is only called when `completedNodeIds` is non-empty at walk start, meaning a true fresh-record resume (empty set) skips it and re-enters rotateOne(root) causing AEAD failure under the old root key

`mergeConcurrentChildren` 'remote-wins' policy during CAS-409 can overwrite an already-rotated child's `readKeySealed` with the pre-rotation version, breaking subsequent navigation for that child (liveness-only, not confidentiality)
`mergeChildren` in `folder/merge.ts` was also a Phase-64 throwing stub alongside the four engine.ts seams — an undocumented fifth seam surfaced by research

89 of 93 sdk-e2e tests are quarantined with `describe.skip` mid-milestone under the comment 'SDK runtime stubbed mid-milestone, re-enable at phase 63-65 consumer re-wire' — the e2e gate only covers 4 runnable tests

`vi.clearAllMocks()` does not drain `mockResolvedValueOnce` queues; switching to `vi.resetAllMocks()` was required in engine.test.ts to prevent leftover queue values from contaminating subsequent test blocks

code.finding: D-02 bug: `sealChildReadKey` sealed under child's own pre-rotation key (misnomer `parentReadKey`); fix moves re-seal out-of-band to the BFS caller at L660-681 under parent's NEW readKey'
D-07 ordering bug: `completedNodeIds.add` fired before `reMintGrantsRootedAt` at L391, marking nodes complete before grant re-mint succeeded
D-07 bug: resume guard short-circuited without calling `verifySubtreeClean`, allowing a partial walk to be treated as complete without verifying IPNS truth
mintFileKeyOnRotate seam filled: mints `fileKey' = generateRandomBytes(32)` for file nodes, returns early for folders; `sealNode` re-seals under readKeyPrime
D-01 fail-closed guard: throws if `nodeIpnsPrivateKey` absent from nodeKeySource; remaining PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY at L394 is write-body role only (Phase 65 scope)
verifySubtreeClean seam filled: returns {isDirty, frontier} by checking IPNS-published SealedChildRef generation against envelope generation
verifySubtreeClean only invoked when `completedNodeIds` is non-empty — fresh-record resume (empty set) bypasses it, requiring Phase-68 durable floor for true crash recovery

Per-node convergence guard: before each rotateOne(N), checks if N's published generation already exceeds enqueued baseline; skips rotateOne and seals/verifies parent link only. Does not cover root node (no parent mirror).
D-02 fix: parent re-seal correctly uses `parentState.parentNewReadKey` (parent's NEW readKey' from its own rotateOne result), not the old key
mergeChildren three-way merge: union-by-ipnsName Map (local first, remote overwrites on conflict = remote-wins), both-sides-deleted base entries pruned
mergeConcurrentChildren: unseals base+remote under old key, delegates to mergeChildren, re-seals merged result under readKeyPrime; wired as CAS-409 merge callback in publishWithCas

@ts-expect-error directive was placed above `await expect(` wrapper instead of directly above the `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish({...})` call — caused 'unused directive' error while real TS2345 fired below
CryptoError was imported from `@cipherbox/core` (wrong package); should be `@cipherbox/crypto`. Test passed at runtime because toThrow(undefined) matches any throw, hiding the import error

workflow: Running two background git operations concurrently causes 'could not write index' from an index.lock race; always wait for one git operation to fully complete before starting the next

lint-staged's automatic stash mechanism can conflict on stash pop and dump content from old pre-existing stashes into the working tree as untracked files; remedy: `git restore STATE.md` and move stash artifacts aside before retrying the commit
The GSD commit helper reliably reports `commit_failed` even when the commit lands successfully — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before any retry

tsup/esbuild builds succeed without type checking; a separate `tsc --noEmit` pass is required to catch TypeScript errors, especially in test files that tsconfig.build.json excludes from the build typecheck
The pattern-mapper subagent does not auto-commit PATTERNS.md; the orchestrator must stage and commit it alongside other planning artifacts
When sending a targeted revision to a planner subagent via SendMessage, instruct it to leave the orchestrator's in-progress file edits untouched in the working tree to avoid git conflicts

CodeRabbit's `coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed` produces findings against the full branch diff; on a 42-commit phase it takes 5-10 minutes and bundles findings in the local terminal output rather than PR threads
The `gh pr edit` command fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL — must patch PR body via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`

Adding `.slice()` when extracting a Uint8Array from a captured array is necessary if a later cleanup helper zeroes array elements in-place — the resume run would receive an all-zeros key and throw CryptoError otherwise

friction: Git index.lock race when committing VALIDATION.md while a background researcher agent was still running its own git operations — 'could not write index' failure with a lint-staged stash left behind

lint-staged stash pop conflict during the 64-01 fixup commit dumped unrelated Phase-3 Playwright files (`tests/e2e/`, `06.1-webapp-automation-testing/`) into the working tree as untracked files, requiring manual git restore + move-aside recovery
GSD commit helper consistently reports `commit_failed` even on successful commits (known false-negative), requiring git log verification after every commit

tsup build gives no type-safety signal — executor 64-01 introduced `@ts-expect-error` directive misplacements and a wrong-package `CryptoError` import that only surfaced via a manual `tsc --noEmit` sweep after the wave

SC#4 success criterion ('without double-bumping') directly contradicted design §4.5 — the criterion was written incorrectly and the 64-07 no-double-bump guard over-constrained the implementation, requiring a user decision to defer rather than attempt a fix
The sdk-e2e gate was weaker than expected: 89/93 tests quarantined mid-milestone, so regressions in `cas.ts`/`registration.ts`/`client.ts` changes were not caught by the e2e suite
CodeRabbit CLI review took ~10 minutes on the 42-commit / +3455-line diff, blocking the PR creation until it completed

The `git stash pop` conflict recovery required understanding which of 3 existing stashes was the problematic one and tracing timestamps to distinguish phase-3 artifact stash from lint-staged auto-stash

Live `shares` API schema cutover: `reMintGrantsRootedAt` transport callbacks are implemented but not wired to the live shares persistence layer — deferred to Phase 66

True fresh-record mid-walk crash recovery: empty `completedNodeIds` resume is not viable until Phase-68 IndexedDB durable floor persists `readKeyPrime` across crashes (todo: `rotation-fresh-record-resume-and-sc4-double-bump.md`)
SC#4 wording fix: 'without double-bumping' contradicts design §4.5; the success criterion should be updated and the convergence guard's root-node gap addressed in Phase 68
